item.title: One notch up, three days before the budget: Moody's lifts Zambia from Caa2 to Caa1 with a positive outlook, and the Treasury says the rating is a means, not an end
item.description: Moody's Ratings raised Zambia's sovereign credit rating to Caa1 on Friday 30 October and kept the outlook positive, the third agency to move the country up since the 2020 default. The Ministry of Finance and National Planning welcomed the decision on Monday 2 November, crediting debt restructuring, fiscal consolidation and a steadier economy, and warning that the rating must be turned into investment and jobs. Situmbeko Musokotwane presents the 2027 budget on Friday 6 November, a week later than first planned.

item.title: 'Working round the clock': State House says the US$200 million fuel relief had to end to protect free education and cash transfers, as oil marketers blame a K5 pipeline mark-up
item.description: Two days after the ERB set petrol at K33.06 and diesel at K34.45, State House spokesman Whitney Mulobela said the President was working to soften the blow, blamed Brent crude at about US$112 a barrel and attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, and explained why the April-to-September tax holiday was not renewed. The Oil Marketing Companies Association says prices will keep climbing unless the pipeline's open-access rules are changed.

item.title: 'Malicious and unfounded': the UPND denies that anyone pushed the Tonse candidate out of Mandevu, as an ECZ commissioner tells Sioma poll staff not to expect a rosy Thursday
item.description: UPND elections chairman Likando Mufalali has rejected the Tonse Alliance's claim that its Mandevu candidate, Daniel Chisenga, was threatened into withdrawing, two days before Adrian Banda is declared MP without a vote. In Sioma, ECZ commissioner McDonald Chipenzi closed poll staff training for the Mbeta ward by-election with a warning that polling stations can be chaotic and a reminder that democracy means hearing views one does not share.

item.title: Antigua, not the President: Haimbe carries Zambia's case to the Commonwealth summit, sits as Vice-Chair of the ministerial action group and lobbies to bring the Youth Centre back
item.description: Foreign Minister Mulambo Haimbe is representing President Hichilema at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda from Sunday 1 to Wednesday 4 November. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs says the delegation will sell the Grow Zambia Agenda to investors, sit as Vice-Chair of the Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group and press Zambia's bid to host the Commonwealth Youth Centre again.

item.title: A surety in the cells: the magistrate orders the State to produce Mulenga Fube on Tuesday, as Binwell Mpundu's bench warrant stands and Kang'ombe sends word he is unwell
item.description: The day set for Binwell Mpundu's sureties to produce him or explain his absence ended with one of them in police custody. The Zambian Observer reports that Magistrate Webster Milumbe directed the State on Monday 2 November to bring former Chilubi MP Mulenga Fube, held at Kabwata Police Station, to court on Tuesday, and gave Christopher Kang'ombe, said to be unwell, another date. Mpundu, wanted on a bench warrant since 13 October in a seditious practices case, has still not appeared.

item.title: K222 million and US$5.7 million in three months: the FIC's second case study describes a business-support company that was really a payment channel
item.description: The Financial Intelligence Centre's 11th Money Laundering Trends Report contains a second worked example that News Diggers and the Rio Times reported on Monday 2 November: five unnamed companies, only one of them a licensed payment provider, moved money across borders under labels such as equipment purchase. The case has been passed to law enforcement; no one has been charged.

item.title: Freddie Mwila, the captain of 1967, the Atlanta Chief who scored twice against Manchester City, and the coach who won Zambia's only continental club title, dies at 80
item.description: Freddie Mwila Snr died at about 01:00 on Monday 2 November at Maina Soko Medical Centre in Lusaka after a stroke, his family said. One of the first Zambians to play professionally abroad, a member of the side that reached the 1974 Africa Cup of Nations final and the coach of Power Dynamos' 1991 African Cup Winners' Cup side, he was 80. Mourners are gathering at the family home at Mapepe Farms in Chilanga.

item.title: Power Dynamos pay the same K100,000 as Nkana, with a three-match Arthur Davies ban held over them, as Kingstone Mutandwa's knee rules him out of the Burundi qualifier
item.description: The FAZ Disciplinary Committee's verdict on political chanting covers both Kitwe clubs: Power Dynamos are fined K100,000 for the 11 October match against Nchanga Rangers and face a suspended three-match ban from Arthur Davies Stadium. Meanwhile the Chipolopolo have lost striker Kingstone Mutandwa to a knee injury suffered with Servette, about eight weeks before the 13 November AFCON qualifier against Burundi at National Heroes Stadium.

item.title: Two ceremonies, two speeches read for the President: Kasune ties Chibuluma's Ikubi Lya Malumbe to five million tourists, and Chief Nyawa's Guta Mweenze hears a promise on palaces
item.description: At the Ikubi Lya Malumbe ceremony of Chief Chibuluma in Mumbwa, Tourism Minister Princess Kasune said heritage is a resource for development as well as identity. At Chief Nyawa's Guta Mweenze in Kazungula, Home Affairs Minister Mancel Ameleki read a presidential speech warning that a divided society cannot grow and promising that no chief will be left without a decent palace. Both were reported by the Times of Zambia.

item.title: Fourteen disappearances and 71 arrests: Human Rights Watch calls for an end to the post-election crackdown, as State House answers Ian Khama and the treason bail ruling nears
item.description: In a report released on Sunday 1 November, Human Rights Watch says Zambian police and soldiers forcibly disappeared, detained, beat and threatened opposition members, lawyers, journalists and critics around the 13 August election, and that Mutotwe Kafwaya's killing has still not been credibly explained. The report lands amid the row over Ian Khama's description of Hakainde Hichilema as a dictator, three days before the High Court rules on bail for Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 others.

item.title: 'I don't have a sense of entitlement': Mweetwa says no MP is owed a ministry, denies planning a new party with other dropped ministers, and stays with the UPND
item.description: Cornelius Mweetwa spent five years as Minister of Information and Media and chief government spokesman. He kept Choma Central in August but was not among the 30 ministers named this week. In remarks carried by Kalemba and the Zambian Observer on Sunday, he said the President chooses on national interest and skills, that the old Cabinet dissolved with the election, and that talk of him forming a party with other left-out ministers is a political fallacy. News Diggers counts him, Rodney Sikumba and Chipoka Mulenga among the reshuffle's casualties.

item.title: Printed before the withdrawals: the 5 November ballot papers land from Dubai with the Mandevu names still on them, six wards prepare to vote, and Lubinda questions Article 52(6)
item.description: The Electoral Commission says the ballot papers for Thursday's by-elections arrived at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport on Saturday, a day late, and that the Mandevu papers carry the names of three candidates who have since withdrawn, because printing finished before their letters arrived. Only six wards in five districts will actually poll; the UPND is unopposed in Mandevu, Lumezi North, the Mbala mayoralty and five wards. Given Lubinda says the constitutional amendment that lets a withdrawal end a contest has left voters without a choice.

item.title: 'An undisclosed location': Emmanuel Banda's mother asks the High Court to make the police produce her son, as a UPND official says his 2024 escape should count against bail
item.description: Grace Nampokolwe Banda says she has not seen or heard from her son since he was apprehended in Mozambique in mid-October, that police stations turned her away on 16 October, and that a letter from her lawyers to the Inspector General has gone unanswered. Her habeas corpus application names the Attorney-General as respondent and says no charge, warrant or detention order has been shown to the family. State House has said the former Petauke Central MP faces attempted murder and aggravated robbery charges and will appear before a court.

item.title: Drones 'sent to Zambia in error': the Economic and Financial Crimes Court at Chongwe convicts GMX Systems Zambia and two men over under-declared imports, with K2.1 million to pay
item.description: The Zambia Revenue Authority says the court convicted GMX Systems Zambia Limited, Aminadav Bardavid and Aaron Ngoma of making false representations and importing goods without customs entries. Prosecutors said invoices understated the value of imported drones and that the two men told the ZRA the consignments were meant for a sister company in Israel. The company was fined K30,000 a count and must pay more than K2.1 million in outstanding tax; Bardavid was fined K380,000 and Ngoma K40,000. Six co-accused were acquitted on every count.

item.title: 'Manifestly inadequate': the prosecution asks the Court of Appeal to lengthen Malanji's four years and Yamba's three and to overturn the hotel acquittal, Kalemba reports
item.description: Kalemba reports, in a story carried by the Zambian Observer on Sunday, that the National Prosecution Authority has filed a cross-appeal against the sentences handed to the former foreign minister Joseph Malanji and the former Secretary to the Treasury Fredson Yamba in September 2025, arguing the trial court should have imposed the statutory maximum, and asking the Court of Appeal to reverse Malanji's acquittal on the Royal Gibson Hotel count. The convictions, sentences and the State's intention to appeal that count are recorded on the NPA's website.

item.title: The 'wandering zone': the Bank of Zambia says a security thread that sits in a slightly different place does not make a banknote counterfeit, and lists the features to check
item.description: In a public notice on Thursday 29 October the central bank explained that the thread is allowed to move within a defined band during production, so that its extra thickness does not build a ridge in a stack of notes. The eagle image can shift slightly too. The bank's assistant director for communications, Besnat Mwanza, urged people to use several features, the watermark, the see-through register, raised print and colour-shifting ink, rather than the thread alone, and pointed to its free Zambian Banknotes app as a guide, not an authenticator.

item.title: Thirty-four bales and the bill for burning them: the standards agency seizes used underwear worth K37,350 from a Lusaka shop and restates the 2006 ban on second-hand undergarments
item.description: The Zambia Compulsory Standards Agency says whistleblowers tipped it off that a Lusaka shop was selling used undergarments, and that officers seized 34 bales valued at K37,350 last week. The shop has been ordered to pay for the consignment's disposal. In a statement on Sunday, the agency's communications manager Brian Hatyoka cited Zambian Standard 559 and Statutory Instrument 120 of 2006, which prohibit the import and sale of used underwear and nightwear, and warned of stern action against traders who ignore them.

item.title: Three from three and a 40-point margin: Munali Suns crush Botswana's Dolphins 96–56 at NASDEC, Douglas Kandulu scores 35, and Harare Kings are next on Monday afternoon
item.description: A day after escaping Ferroviario da Beira by two points, the Lusaka side produced a 40-point win. They led 50–25 at half-time, ran off 16 unanswered points, shot 50 per cent to the Dolphins' 31, and now sit alone at the top of the six-team group on three wins from three. Beira and the Dolphins are both 2–1. The top two go to the Elite 16 in Nairobi from 23 November. The Suns play Harare Kings at 16:00 on Monday and Soweto Panthers after that.

item.title: Five draws from six and a goalless Kitwe derby: Zanaco are the only winners of Super League week six, while Fashion Sakala scores and makes two for Al-Fayha
item.description: Seven goals in six matches on Saturday 31 October, and five of them in Solwezi. Power Dynamos and Nkana shared a 0–0 at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium, Green Eagles, ZESCO United, Red Arrows and FC MUZA all drew blank, and Zanaco's 3–2 at Trident was the only win of the round. MUZA lead Stream A on 11 points, Green Eagles Stream B on the same. In Saudi Arabia, Fashion Sakala scored, set up two more and was named player of the match as Al-Fayha beat Al-Faisaly 4–1.

item.title: Petrol K33.06, diesel K34.45: the ERB raises every fuel price for November on a weaker kwacha and Gulf tensions, a day after Nalumango ruled out using reserves at the pump
item.description: A month after the K6 jump that followed the end of the tax relief, the Energy Regulation Board has added K1.60 to petrol and K1.18 to diesel from midnight on Saturday 31 October. Kerosene goes to K32.08 and Jet A-1 to K34.51. The board says international prices rose for petrol and kerosene and the kwacha lost more than 3 per cent; diesel went up even though its international price fell. On Friday Mutale Nalumango told Parliament the country's US$6.5 billion in reserves would not be used for fuel.

item.title: No ballot in Mandevu: the ECZ will declare Adrian Banda MP on 5 November, Tonse asks for a rerun with a new candidate, and Nalumango says a retreating opposition could gift 2031
item.description: The Electoral Commission's public notice of Friday 30 October ends the Mandevu contest without a vote: with the FDD's Daniel Chisenga, the Leadership Movement's Ntazana Mutungwa and the independent Daniel Daka out, the UPND's Adrian Banda is the only validly nominated candidate and will be declared elected. The Tonse Alliance wants the poll cancelled so it can field someone else. In Parliament, Mutale Nalumango mocked the withdrawals; Citizens First's Harry Kalaba said she had a point.

item.title: Fertiliser, irrigation and 10,000 megawatts: in Moscow, Haimbe reads Hichilema's pitch to Russian investors and asks for help with climate preparedness and African-language AI
item.description: President Hichilema did not travel to the Third Russia-Africa Summit, but his speech did. Delivered at the plenary by Foreign Affairs Minister Mulambo Haimbe, it offered Russian capital a place in fertiliser production, irrigation technology and the power build-out under the Grow Zambia Agenda, repeated the targets of three million tonnes of copper and ten million tonnes of maize, and asked for cooperation on climate adaptation, artificial intelligence and reform of the UN Security Council.

item.title: 12,637 cases in ninety days: police record a rise in gender-based violence for the third quarter, with 2,751 child victims, 49 murders and Lusaka and Luapula top of the table
item.description: The Zambia Police Service's quarterly statement, issued on Friday 30 October by spokesperson Chipo Kaitisha, counts 7,972 criminal and 4,665 non-criminal GBV cases between July and September. Women and girls were 80.5 per cent of victims. Child victims rose by 433 on the same quarter of 2025 and murders from 30 to 49. The total is also up on the 10,881 cases the police recorded for April to June.

item.title: 'Not a registered entity': the Chitimukulu asks the Constitutional Court to throw out the petition to make Chief Mukuni a paramount chief, saying the committee behind it cannot sue
item.description: Paramount Chief Chitimukulu Henry Kanyanta Sosala has filed a summons to dismiss the petition brought in June by the Bene Mukuni Royal Dynasty Committee through its director-general, Jonas Shakafuswa, for want of capacity and jurisdiction. His affidavit says searches at PACRA and the registrars of societies and NGOs on 16 October found no such registered body, and that only the holder of a chief's office can sue over its status.

item.title: Africa's first oral cholera vaccine plant breaks ground in November, the President says, as the outbreak that prompted a 709,000-dose campaign stands at 1,622 cases and 30 deaths
item.description: The Zambia Daily Mail reported on Friday 30 October that President Hichilema, speaking as he swore in his last two ministers, said construction of the vaccine plant at the Lusaka South Multi-Facility Economic Zone would start next month, with a planned 20 million doses a year. The project dates from a 2024 memorandum with a Chinese manufacturer. The Health Minister's latest figures put the outbreak at 1,622 cases in 20 districts since 28 July.

item.title: Champions of Tier B: Zambia's under-15s beat Portugal 5–2 in Baku, Maxen Msimuko scores a hat-trick in the final, and Keith Mweemba tells the squad FAZ will manage what comes next
item.description: The first FIFA U-15 World Cup ended for Zambia with a trophy on Friday 30 October. Brian Kunsanama's side, placed in Tier B after finishing second in their group, beat England, Niger, Slovakia and Senegal on the way to the final and then Portugal 5–2, with Msimuko's three goals taking him to 16 for the tournament by ZamFoot's count. The result places Zambia 33rd of 189 teams overall.

item.title: Two from two at NASDEC: Munali Suns beat Bravehearts and come from ten down against Beira, and meet Botswana's Dolphins on Sunday afternoon with a place in the Elite 16 the prize
item.description: Zambia's champions opened the Road to BAL 2027 group in Lusaka with a 79–66 win over Malawi's Bravehearts on Friday and an 87–85 recovery against Ferroviario da Beira on Saturday, Douglas Kandulu posting 21 points, 13 rebounds and five blocks. They and the Dolphins are the only unbeaten sides in Group E; the top two go to the East Division Elite 16 in Nairobi from 23 November.

item.title: A K100,000 fine and a ban held in reserve: FAZ's disciplinary committee punishes Nkana for the political chants of 10 October but suspends the five-match exile from Kitwe
item.description: Three weeks after a section of the crowd at Nkana Stadium sang the campaign song of the detained opposition figures during the 4–1 win over Makeni All Stars, the Football Association of Zambia has ruled. Nkana are fined K100,000 and ordered to play five home games behind closed doors at least 300 km away, but the committee suspended the ban in view of the club's remorse. Nkana say they respect the decision and have asked their supporters to stop.

item.title: A debate at Kaunda's old house earns two Lusaka schools a trip to Uganda, and the heritage commission says it turned a complaint about motorbikes into an exchange programme
item.description: Learners from Kamwala Secondary and Libala Stage 3 Secondary who debated at Chilenje House during the Independence celebrations have been offered an educational exchange in Uganda by the visiting Afrika Mashariki Fest Group, Zambia Monitor reports. The National Heritage Conservation Commission's Kagosi Mwamulowe said the offer showed what a monument could do beyond standing still.

item.title: 'This is the last adjournment': Mundubile, Zulu and 16 others appear at last, and the High Court sets 5 November for the bail hearing as the State asks for time to read the reply
item.description: All 18 applicants were brought from Mukobeko to the Lusaka High Court on Thursday 29 October, but the constitutional bail application still did not start. The Attorney-General asked for time to study the defence's 32-paragraph reply; the bench adjourned to 09:00 on Thursday 5 November and, the defence says, warned it would rule on the papers if either side was not ready. The State's affidavit argues two months in custody is not unreasonable for treason and terrorism charges and calls Mundubile and Zulu flight risks.

item.title: One name left on the Mandevu ballot: all three of Adrian Banda's rivals withdraw a week before polling day, and the FDD's Daniel Chisenga says threats to his family forced him out
item.description: Letters dated Wednesday 28 October from the FDD's Daniel Chisenga, the Leadership Movement's candidate and the independent Daniel Daka reached the Electoral Commission a week before the Mandevu re-run on Thursday 5 November, leaving the UPND's Adrian Banda as the only candidate. Chisenga, the Tonse Alliance's man, says threats began on nomination day and spread to his family; the UPND said earlier this month it knew of no threats and that weak opponents should withdraw. The ECZ has not announced a declaration.

item.title: The last two desks filled: Milupi takes Transport and Logistics, Kalila takes Housing with an order that councils allocate only serviced land, and Mulusa returns as Chief Whip
item.description: A day after swearing in 24 ministers, President Hichilema completed the line-up on Thursday 29 October: Charles Milupi to Transport and Logistics, with instructions to move on the Lobito Corridor, TAZARA and Zambia Railways without delay, and Christopher Kalila to the new Ministry of Housing, told to tackle unplanned settlements by putting roads and sanitation in before plots are handed out. In Parliament the Speaker announced that Solwezi North's Stafford Mulusa is Government Chief Whip again, with Matero's Alexander Sakala as his deputy.

item.title: Inflation edges up to 6.3 per cent as diesel jumps 24 per cent in a month, and September's trade balance swings to a US$186 million deficit on weaker copper exports
item.description: ZamStats' October bulletin, released in Lusaka on Thursday 29 October, puts annual inflation at 6.3 per cent, up from 6.1, with food inflation easing to 5.7 per cent and non-food rising to 7.4. The price table explains why: diesel up 23.8 per cent and petrol up 24.4 per cent in a month, while a 25 kg bag of breakfast meal is a tenth cheaper than a year ago. Exports fell 8.1 per cent in September and imports rose 5.4 per cent, turning August's US$48 million surplus into a US$186.4 million deficit as refined copper earnings dropped 15 per cent.

item.title: US$31 billion to 2050 and a US$23.1 billion hole for ZESCO: the Energy Ministry's financing strategy for the power plan, as the Permanent Secretary puts capacity at 4,722 MW
item.description: The Ministry of Energy's financing strategy for the Integrated Resource Plan, presented at a Centre for Trade Policy and Development meeting in Lusaka and reported by Zambia Monitor, says the plan needs about US$31 billion by 2050 and US$11.6 billion by 2030, roughly US$1.07 billion a year against concessional flows averaging US$231 million. Under an open-access market, ZESCO could face a gap of up to US$23.1 billion between 2033 and 2050. Separately, Permanent Secretary Arnold Simwaba put installed capacity at 4,722 MW, up from 3,777 MW in 2024.

item.title: 1,622 cases and 30 deaths, more than half of them before reaching a clinic: Chilengi tells Parliament the outbreak has spread to 20 districts as 709,018 people are vaccinated
item.description: In a ministerial statement to the National Assembly on Thursday 29 October, Health Minister Roma Chilengi said Zambia had recorded 1,622 cholera cases and 30 deaths since 28 July, 16 of the deaths in communities before patients reached a health facility. The outbreak covers 20 districts in six provinces, Mumbwa and Chisamba the latest; Lusaka Province accounts for 1,090 cases. The Treasury has released K13 million for emergency water supply, and 709,018 people, 91 per cent of the target, have been vaccinated in Lusaka, Chibombo and Chongwe.

item.title: Mapatizya falls vacant: the High Court at Livingstone nullifies Emeldah Munashabantu's election over the ECZ's handling of the count, finds the MP blameless and awards costs
item.description: Judge Kazimbe Chenda has set aside the 13 August election of the UPND's Emeldah Munashabantu in Mapatizya, Zimba District, on the petition of independent Clive Miyanda, the Zambian Observer reported on Thursday evening, citing Mwebantu. The judgment is reported to dismiss the misconduct allegation against the MP but to find that the ECZ did not conduct the post-voting process substantially in accordance with electoral law after violence at the Kabanga totalling centre. The ECZ is to pay the petitioner's costs. An appeal is open.

item.title: A final in Baku: Zambia's under-15s beat Slovakia 3–1 and Senegal 4–3 in one day and meet Portugal for the Tier B title on Friday, with Maxen Msimuko on 13 goals
item.description: Two knockout wins on Thursday 29 October took the Junior Chipolopolo to the Tier B final of the first FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival. Slovakia were beaten 3–1 in the quarter-final, and in the semi-final Zambia came from behind three times against Senegal, Moses Munkombwe, Maxen Msimuko twice and Samuel Musonda scoring in a 4–3 win, ZamFoot reported. Msimuko has 13 goals in the tournament and Musonda scored one and set up two in the semi. The final against Portugal is at the Crystal Hall on Friday 30 October, one of four finals with an African side.

item.title: Maniema Union, Singida Black Stars and a club still to be decided: Red Arrows learn their Confederation Cup group, with the first matches from 27 November
item.description: The draw in Cairo on Wednesday 28 October put Red Arrows in Group C of the TotalEnergies CAF Confederation Cup with AS Maniema Union of DR Congo, Singida Black Stars of Tanzania and the winner of an unresolved qualifier among CR Belouizdad, AS Douanes and Hafia. It is the Zambian champions' first group stage in the competition, reached by beating Kaizer Chiefs on penalties. The group stage opens on the weekend of 27 to 29 November and ends in late January, with the top two in each group going to the quarter-finals in February.

item.title: Six for Senegal: a judoka, a badminton player, three swimmers and a sprinter carry Zambia into the first Olympic event held in Africa, which opens in Dakar on Saturday
item.description: The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games open on Saturday 31 October and run to 13 November. Zambia's team, sent off at the Senegalese embassy in Lusaka on 25 October, is Elisha Zimba in judo, Bhardwaj Anjuman in badminton, Sibongile Miti, Joshua Mulenga and Edward Cole in swimming and Nathan Matete in athletics, with Besa Chibwe as chef de mission. The National Olympic Committee says it applied for 115 places and was allocated six, and that Zambia has won four medals, one of them gold, at three previous Youth Games.

item.title: Twenty-four ministers in an afternoon: Hichilema fills the 30-ministry Cabinet, gives Tambatamba the mines and splits Energy between Kapala and Chikote
item.description: A day after Parliament approved the new structure, President Hakainde Hichilema swore in 24 Cabinet ministers at State House on Wednesday 28 October, filling the posts left empty since August. Brenda Tambatamba moves from Labour to Mines, Peter Kapala and Makozo Chikote take the new Electricity and Petroleum ministries, Felix Mutati and Douglas Syakalima return, and Jack Mwiimbu moves from Home Affairs to Justice. Fred M'membe called the expansion out of touch; Highvie Hamududu called its cost insignificant.

item.title: A week's grace for the new ministers: the 2027 budget moves from Friday to 6 November, and the Vice-President says the government is 'still working on it'
item.description: Vice-President Mutale Nalumango told Parliament on Tuesday 27 October that Situmbeko Musokotwane will now present the 2027 national budget on Friday 6 November rather than 30 October, News Diggers reports. The change came the day before 24 ministers were sworn in, and after Citizens First argued that ministers appointed on a Wednesday could not defend a budget on the Friday. ZIPAR, meanwhile, has asked the Treasury not to cut PAYE.

item.title: K4.1 billion paid, K14.6 billion still owed: Musokotwane says most maize farmers will be paid in November once the Treasury releases K14.7 billion, and the FRA has export contracts
item.description: In a ministerial statement on Tuesday 27 October the acting Agriculture Minister said the Food Reserve Agency had bought 2.7 million tonnes of maize worth K18.738 billion from 1,850 depots this season, far above its 500,000-tonne target, and had so far paid K4.1 billion of it. The balance is to come from the supplementary budget, with most payments expected next month, Zambia Monitor and the Zambia Daily Mail report.

item.title: US$1.8 billion of suspected illicit flows, 580 tax cases and a shell company that turned K85 million into a K150 million contract: what the FIC's 2025 trends report says
item.description: The Financial Intelligence Centre's eleventh money laundering trends report puts suspected illicit financial flows at US$1.8 billion in 2025, down from US$3.5 billion in 2024, with 786 intelligence reports passed to law enforcement, most of them over suspected tax evasion by shell companies. Zambia Monitor and News Diggers report that ZRA assessments arising from the Centre's work exceeded K12.5 billion.

item.title: 'We are around US$20 billion plus': Hichilema asks a Swiss trade mission to invest beyond copper and in joint ventures with Zambians, and thanks Bern for its part in the debt deal
item.description: A Swiss business delegation led by State Secretary Helene Artieda called at State House on Tuesday 27 October. The President urged investment beyond traditional minerals and said foreign investors should partner local businesses, arguing that joint ownership protects against expropriation; Artieda said Switzerland backs the Grow Zambia Agenda and is exploring a government-to-government platform for Swiss companies, the Zambia Daily Mail and News Diggers report.

item.title: A petition to scrap the two-term limit reaches Parliament through a UPND MP, Kabimba tells the President to silence those behind it, and the Attorney-General says time will tell
item.description: The Zambia Youth Organisation Consortium handed nominated MP Francis Kope a petition on Tuesday 27 October asking Parliament to abolish presidential term limits and drop the Grade 12 requirement for candidates; Kope said he would start the process of bringing it to the House, the Zambia Daily Mail and News Diggers report. Economic Front leader Wynter Kabimba said the President should tell those pushing a third term to 'shut up'.

item.title: Third time, still not started: the High Court orders Mukobeko to produce Mundubile, Zulu and 16 others at 10:00 on Thursday after the defence asks for time to answer the State
item.description: The constitutional bail application by Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 co-accused failed to get under way for a third time on Wednesday 28 October, Zambia Monitor reports. The defence asked for time to reply to the State's affidavit in opposition, served on Tuesday evening, and the applicants were again not brought from prison; the three-judge panel ordered them produced on Thursday morning and warned the officer in charge to appear and explain any failure.

item.title: Two down and then three up: Zambia's under-15s come back to beat England 3–2 in Baku and reach the last 16 of the first FIFA U-15 World Cup
item.description: England led 2–0 at the Hovsan complex on Wednesday 28 October before Maxen Msimuko pulled one back before half-time, Samuel Musonda equalised and Chrispine Katoba scored the winner, ZamFoot reports. Brian Kunsanama's side, who finished second in their group on 12 points, now wait to learn their round-of-16 opponent in the tournament's Tier 2 competition.

item.title: Heroes is open for November: CAF grants the National Heroes Stadium temporary Category 3 approval, bringing the Burundi qualifier to Lusaka on 13 November and the U-23s' tie after
item.description: A CAF letter dated 28 October, following an inspection from 19 to 22 October, gives the Lusaka stadium temporary approval to host international matches in November, ZamFoot reports. The Chipolopolo's 2027 AFCON qualifier against Burundi moves from Levy Mwanawasa Stadium to Heroes on 13 November, and the under-23s play Burkina Faso there on 15 November, with CAF listing concerns still to be addressed before a further assessment.

item.title: A ministry of its own: Christopher Chibuye of Mkushi North becomes the first Minister of Culture and Arts, five years after the arts were folded into Youth and Sport
item.description: Among the 24 ministers sworn in on Wednesday 28 October is the first head of a stand-alone Ministry of Culture and Arts, created when Parliament dissolved the Ministry of Youth, Sport and Arts on Tuesday. The Vice-President told the House that culture and arts should be seen as an economic opportunity that can draw tourists and create jobs; the sector's new minister is a Mkushi North MP who came to the UPND from the PF.

item.title: Thirty ministries and two familiar faces: Parliament approves Hichilema's realignment a day after it was tabled, as Felix Mutati and Douglas Syakalima are nominated and sworn in
item.description: The National Assembly adopted the Vice-President's motion on Tuesday 27 October, clearing the way for a government of 30 ministries built around separate portfolios for Electricity, Petroleum, Trade and Exports, Industry, Housing and Skills and Higher Education. News Diggers reports that the President has nominated two former ministers to Parliament and that the Speaker swore them in. The published documents carry no cost estimate, and whether Friday's budget presentation still stands was not confirmed.

item.title: 'I am surprised there is no Ministry of Ministers': the cost argument over 30 ministries, and the case made for Electricity, Petroleum, Housing and Culture
item.description: Chapter One Foundation asked Parliament to test whether the realignment is necessary and affordable, Brian Mushimba said Zambia needs consolidation rather than more bureaucracy, and Laura Miti asked how rural voters benefit. On the other side, Sunday Chanda argued that each new portfolio answers a real problem and Greyford Monde made the case for a dedicated electricity ministry.

item.title: Leave PAYE alone, put 15 per cent into health, or do not present it at all: the asks pile up ahead of a 2027 budget scheduled for Friday
item.description: ZIPAR told a briefing on Monday that the government should not cut the PAYE rate because the Grow Zambia Agenda needs the revenue; the Resident Doctors Association wants health's share lifted from about 13 per cent to at least 15; and Citizens First wants the whole presentation held back until there is a Cabinet to defend it. The business statement of 24 October set the presentation for Friday 30 October.

item.title: A 150 MW coal plant for Ndola and 245 MWp of solar for Mufulira and Kasama: the ERB clears 61 licences and permits worth K13.4 billion in proposed investment
item.description: The Energy Regulation Board's licensing committee met on 14 October and approved 48 licence applications, nine construction permits and four amendments to petroleum transport licences, covering about US$662.3 million of proposed spending across electricity, renewables and downstream petroleum, according to a statement reported by two energy trade outlets on Tuesday.

item.title: 5,595 confiscated, 27 found: the Mpika North MP calls the Auditor-General's report a crime scene and demands an investigation into the missing Mukula logs
item.description: Francis Kapyanga says the government must account for 5,568 Mukula logs that the Mpika District Forestry Office recorded as confiscated between 2021 and 2025 but which a physical inspection in May 2026 could not find. The Auditor-General's 2025 report, which carries the finding, says the value of the missing logs could not be established.

item.title: A train held at Mapepe: 25 passengers on the Kitwe–Livingstone service taken to the Chilanga treatment centre, as the national count passes 1,480 cases and 29 deaths
item.description: Zambia Railways stopped passenger train 601 in the Chilanga area on Monday 26 October after a passenger fell ill with vomiting and diarrhoea; the Times of Zambia reports that 25 of about 500 people on board showed cholera symptoms and that 500 vaccine doses were brought to the train. ZNPHI's update the same day gave 68 new cases, one death and a cumulative 1,488 cases.

item.title: Out after eleven days: the High Court grants Lima MP Kelvin Kaunda K30,000 bail on an assault charge, the Zambian Observer reports, as he denies 'widespread violence' in court
item.description: Kaunda, the NRPUP member for the new Lima constituency, was arrested at the High Court on 15 October and held at Lubwa police post and then Mwembeshi Prison despite meeting police bond conditions. Judge Kaumbi Ndulo had ordered the State to produce him on Monday 27 October; the Zambian Observer reported that evening that bail was granted. He is also the respondent in an election petition in which he gave evidence on Monday.

item.title: Four wins, 22 goals and a seven-goal afternoon for Maxen Msimuko: Zambia's under-15s finish second in their group at the first FIFA U-15 World Cup and go into Tier B
item.description: The Junior Chipolopolo beat Comoros 3–2 on Monday to close Group X with wins over Tanzania, Moldova, Montserrat and Comoros and a single defeat to Uruguay, finishing level on 12 points with the group winners. As runners-up they play on in Tier B of a 189-team, eight-a-side festival in Baku, with round two on Wednesday and the finals on Friday.

item.title: Chulu and Mbevya win in Monze as MO Drive take a one-two in round three of the national rally championship, with Zain Sidique still leading the standings
item.description: The Afrivert Energy Monze Motor Rally ran more than 91 km of gravel and plantation stages over the weekend of 24–25 October, backed by a K300,000 sponsorship pool. Geoffrey Chulu and navigator Kapuzya Mbevya won from team-mates Charles Hanankuni and Lweendo Simunzele, with the father-and-son Mukosa crew third. The title is decided at the final round in late November.

item.title: 'Ministry on wheels': the President delivers the bus he promised Adventist youth at July's Big Sabbath, and the Lusaka Conference asks its members to keep praying for him
item.description: Pastor Francis Chibiya, president of the Seventh-day Adventist Church's Lusaka Conference, unveiled the vehicle pledged by President Hichilema on 27 July at the Blessing Centre. The bus will carry Pathfinders to camporees and young people to retreats and evangelistic campaigns; the church did not give its cost or capacity.

item.title: Redrawing the ministries before naming the ministers: Hichilema asks Parliament to approve the creation, merger and dissolution of ministries, with Nalumango to move the motion
item.description: State House said on Monday 26 October that President Hakainde Hichilema has written to the National Assembly under Article 92(2)(d) of the Constitution seeking approval for a realignment of government ministries, which it says will put the machinery of government behind the Grow Zambia Agenda. Vice-President Mutale Nalumango will move the motion. No ministry has yet been named, no date set, and the request lands with a Cabinet of four ministers two and a half months after the election.
